- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥ 0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly, especially after recent spikes.
- When sentiment is negative (≤ -0.33) or mixed, model often underestimates; adjust upward, particularly if recent price is rising.
- Model frequently overreacts to short-term sentiment shifts — if sentiment flips sharply, delay or dampen forecast adjustment for 1–2 periods.
- Overshoots after price spikes (especially >70) are common; cap forecast at +5–10% above peak unless sentiment strongly supports continuation.
- Mean reversion bias: if forecast is >10% above recent 5-day average, reduce by 1–2% per day until convergence.
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to underestimate late-period (last 7–10 days) price action — increase forecast by 1–3% for final 5–7 days if sentiment is bullish.
- If sentiment history shows repeated “reversal” patterns (e.g., +0.33 → -0.33 → +0.33), model often misjudges direction — align forecast with sentiment trend, not absolute value.
